newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sale of Brazil Coelce stake to proceed.
newsitem.headline: Sale of Brazil Coelce stake to proceed.

text.p: The sale of a 15 percent stake in Ceara state power utility Coelce will proceed today after a court ruled against a legal challenge by electrical workers seeking to halt the auction, a bolsa spokeswoman said.

"That injunction request was decided in favor of the auction," a spokeswoman for the Fortaleza Stock Exchange in the northerneastern Brazilian state told Reuters. "The auction is scheduled to go forward."
Ceara hopes to sell 22.2 billion preferred shares at an auction slated for 1330 local time/1230 EDT on the regional bourse in an initial step towards privatizing the firm.
The sale also is intended to create a more liquid market for the shares. Coelce is slated to be privatized in the first quarter of 1998.
The bourse spokeswoman said the government has set a minimum price of 3.30 reais a share for the A series stock.
Coelce's preferred A share was up 2.33 percent at 4.40 reais at 1230 local time/1130 EDT on the Sao Paulo bourse, while its illiquid preferred B was untraded after closing September 20 at 0.82 real.
The sell-off was originally slated for earlier this week but was delayed by a court injunction, which has since been overturned.
On Thursday, the Electrical Workers of Ceara union had filed for an injunction, but a judge today ruled against the request.
